His repeated statements such as, "Main try karta hoon, Diwan aapko jaldi aa jayega" and "I will continuously follow up with them" gave us confidence to proceed with the purchase.

While two of the products were delivered on time, the third product, a Diwan, was scheduled for delivery on 29.05.2026.

On 20.05.2026, I contacted Mr. Aziz to check whether the Diwan had been shipped and requested him to help ensure delivery on or before 29.05.2026. However, he neither answered my calls nor responded to my messages. Later, I learned through his message that he would be on leave for the next 15 days due to personal reasons. Upon speaking with Mr. Swarup, I was informed that the Diwan would not be delivered on 29.05.2026 due to a quality-check issue from their end. What was even more disappointing was the casual manner in which the matter was handled, with the response simply being, "Diwan deliver nahi hoga aaj."

After several follow-ups and repeated requests, the Diwan was finally delivered on 04.06.2026, forcing me to reschedule my plans.

However, no one arrived, and there was no communication regarding the delay. Eventually, I had to arrange and pay for my own carpenter to complete the assembly.

Overall, this was a highly disappointing experience marked by unfulfilled commitments, poor communication, lack of accountability, and inadequate customer service. I would not recommend this store to anyone.

I placed this order because I have an international flight next week and needed to carry the item with me abroad. The delay and cancellation have put me in a very difficult situation.

Additionally, I was asked via WhatsApp to pay INR 2500 for delivery charges, even though your website clearly states free delivery. This inconsistency is unacceptable and feels misleading.

In contrast, I placed an order with The Bombay Store, and they delivered the very next day without charging any extra delivery fees. I have been their customer since 2015 and have always had a reliable experience. This situation clearly shows the difference in professionalism and customer service.

If I had been informed earlier about the issue, I would have ordered from another website and avoided this inconvenience. Because of this delay and cancellation, I am now unable to bring the Hindu deity with me as planned.

I sincerely hope you review your customer service, communication practices, and delivery policies so other customers do not face similar disappointment.

I had got an antique map framed at Satguru’s Andheri last year. I paid a 3x premium over local framers on the basis that I will get premium quality and service. To my shock, fungus has seeped in through the frame and spoilt the map within a year. There is no particular dampness or moisture on the wall where the map was kept.

When I went to Satguru’s Andheri, they said they can’t do anything about it and I need to visit Satguru’s Khar. At Satguru’s Khar, they said there will be an INR 5,000/- extra charge to replace the wood at the back of the frame(!). I wasn’t expecting free service, but looking to charge so much a year after I purchased the frame and making me run around from Andheri to Khar has made this a bitter experience. On top of this, there was zero sympathy or service etiquette from the owner or staff- all they were looking to do was to argue that it wasn’t their fault and they bore no responsibility for this.

I will never buy anything from Satguru’s again and would encourage others to also look at alternative options which offer better service and value than Satguru’s.

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Aman Bhonsle
featured_reviews.review_text:
I’ve spent a decade in Southeast Asia. I’ve seen how cultural centres work there. Not just as venues, but as ecosystems. Programming, audiences, and moderation move together. Momentum is built deliberately.

In that context, this space feels timely. Important, even.

So I walked into this short film event with my wife. Hopeful.

And credit where it’s due. The space is beautifully put together. Thoughtful. Inviting. Clearly built by people who care. The audience was tuned in.

All the right ingredients were there.

Where the evening struggled was in the films.

Several of the works felt giddy and amateur. Technically rough. Narratively unfocused. Distractingly underdeveloped.

One film had incoherent audio. Meaning became guesswork, not interpretation.

Another leaned hard into abstraction. Not out of necessity. More like a shortcut. It tried, sheepishly, to channel Lynch or Nolan but landed closer to a junky home video.

Abstraction isn’t the problem. Effort is effort.

Not every film needs to be “Inception”.

But abstraction without craft, clarity, or purpose turns into obfuscation.

The stories strained for depth instead of arriving at it. The result wasn’t mystery. It was work that felt unfinished and flat.

This isn’t the venue’s fault.

But programming work of this quality undermines both the space and the audience who has paid money to be there.

Then came the Q&A.
This is where things felt uncomfortable for me.

One filmmaker seemed drunk on his own mythology. Cocky. Dismissive. Actively discouraging questions. He spoke as if the audience owed him their attention. No respect for their presence or participation. A bad attitude. Plain and simple. He talked about not wanting to make the film. About being drunk through the conception and writing process. No self-awareness. No sense that he was poisoning the room.

It left a sour taste. Which is a shame.

A space this carefully crafted deserves better stewardship of its conversations.

Another film’s “representative” wasn’t even a filmmaker. It was a producer. Someone who hadn’t been at the shoot. Didn’t understand the technical process. Couldn’t answer basic questions.

Why seat someone like that for a Q&A?

The engagement collapsed. Limp. Unsatisfying.

I come from filmmaking and television. I expected some juice.

Back-and-forth.
War stories.
Love of the craft.
Obsession.

Instead, the interactions felt evasive. Hollow. And the films, frankly, had the roughness of poorly made student projects. Which is wild, considering how sharp even simple YouTube and Instagram reels look today.

You can’t blame everything on the venue.
But curation matters. A lot.

Not all events are created equal.

Their Instagram shows a genuine celebration of life and creativity. That’s why I’m willing to believe this was a one-off misstep. Still, it was our first experience of the space.

There were smaller issues too.

The welcome could’ve been warmer. If there’s an event, don’t leave people outside like they’re waiting for a bus. A few extra chairs wouldn’t hurt.

No water. No tea. No snacks.

An odd hosting choice—though the upcoming café sounds promising.

This is a new space. It’s finding its footing.

What’s already been built is impressive.
The foundation is solid.

The trajectory is familiar to me as I’ve watched cultural districts in Osaka, Spain, Taipei, Thailand, Seoul and Singapore flourish during my visits there.

Early experimentation.
Then sharper programming.
Then confidence.

That’s the game.

I’ll return eventually.

This first visit had gaps.
But it also showed promise.

With tighter curation, stronger moderation and better audience care, this space could become a genuine cultural anchor for the city.
